page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.55 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, alongside 64.0 GB of system memory. This establishes a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Cryptographic instructions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI are supported, alongside AVX, though AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent.

Benchmark testing situates the instance consistently within the middle performance tiers for compute tasks. It achieved a multi-core Geekbench score of 8861.0, a single-core score of 1536.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 21235.7. Cache-resident memory operations perform steadily, registering 1033.55 GB/sec on 16 KB read tests. However, large-block memory operations reveal hardware bottlenecks, falling into the bottom 25% across platforms with 39.33 GB/sec uncached reads and 18.82 GB/sec writes on 256 MB test blocks. In inference testing, smaller models demonstrate responsive generation rates of 307.15 tokens per second on a 135M model, though larger models scale back to average throughput levels.

The ecs.g7a.4xlarge does not include local disk storage or hardware GPU acceleration, requiring external network-attached cloud disks for persistent storage needs. Network bandwidth is provisioned at a 7 Gbps baseline. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides steady, dedicated core performance suitable for mid-tier horizontal scaling without paying for premium specialized silicon. Primary workload fits include enterprise web application serving, backend microservices, moderate Redis caching clusters, and CI/CD compilation pipelines.

Maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the configuration is tailored for balanced operational needs. Benchmark testing reflects average compute output, logging a PassMark CPU score of 21235.7 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8861.0. While small-block memory reads operate solidly at 1033.55 GB/sec, large uncached transfers display reduced throughput at 39.33 GB/sec. The instance includes 7 Gbps baseline network bandwidth but provides zero local storage and no GPU accelerators. The ecs.g7a.4xlarge functions primarily as a stable platform for standard enterprise workloads, including web servers, backend application services, Redis key-value stores, and distributed build pipelines.
